title: Two types of bodies in one background: equal fall and equal clock response

key_results.statement: Response per label and background acceleration of a type: $\varrho_i=g_{\eta,i}$ and $A^{(i)}_{k,\sigma}=\frac{d_{0,i}\tau_i^2}{M^{(i)}_k}(\sigma\mathcal F_i-m_ig_{m,i}-d^{(i)}_kg_{\eta,i})$.
$A^{(i)}_{k,+}$ is the same for all levels iff $\mathcal F_i=m_i(g_{m,i}-g_{\eta,i})$; the value is $-d_{0,i}\tau_i^2g_{\eta,i}=-v_i^2\varrho_i/d_{0,i}$.

Under the unit change $\lambda\to s\lambda$ and $X\to tX$: $\tau_i\to\tau_i/s$, $\kappa_i\to\kappa_i/(st)$, $d_{0,i}\to d_{0,i}/s$, $v_i\to v_i/s^2$, $\varrho_i$ unchanged, $\varrho_i/d_{0,i}\to s\varrho_i/d_{0,i}$, $A^{(i)}_{k,+}\to A^{(i)}_{k,+}/s^3$, $A^{(i)}_{k,+}/v_i^2\to sA^{(i)}_{k,+}/v_i^2$; only $\varrho_i$ is well defined, all ratios between the two types are.

The two types fall alike from rest iff each satisfies $\mathcal F_i=m_i(g_{m,i}-g_{\eta,i})$ and $\kappa_1\tau_1^2g_{\eta,1}=\kappa_2\tau_2^2g_{\eta,2}\neq0$, equivalently $v_1^2\varrho_1/d_{0,1}=v_2^2\varrho_2/d_{0,2}\neq0$.
One acceleration for all levels, both branches and both types iff $\mathcal F_i=0$, $g_{m,i}=g_{\eta,i}$ for $i=1,2$ and $v_1^2\varrho_1/d_{0,1}=v_2^2\varrho_2/d_{0,2}\neq0$.

The accelerations in position labels are equal for all levels of both types iff each type satisfies $\mathcal F_i=m_i(g_{m,i}-g_{\eta,i})$ and $\tau_1^2g_{\eta,1}=\tau_2^2g_{\eta,2}$; the statement is well defined but coincides with falling alike only for $\kappa_1=\kappa_2$.
Clocks respond alike per label iff $g_{\eta,1}=g_{\eta,2}$, and per distance iff $g_{\eta,1}/\kappa_1=g_{\eta,2}/\kappa_2$; only the second compares over the same distance of the background.

If the types fall alike, the clocks respond alike per distance iff $v_1=v_2$; if the clocks respond alike per distance, the types fall alike iff each type falls level-independently, $\varrho_1\neq0$ and $v_1=v_2$.
Controls with $\kappa_1=\kappa_2$, $\tau_2=2\tau_1$ in the variant (a): $g_1=4g_2\neq0$ falls alike with different clock responses; $g_1=g_2\neq0$ has equal clock responses and $A^{(2)}=4A^{(1)}$.

For a sharp stationary field, $C(\Psi\otimes\varphi)=((C_{\rm red}+e_f)\Psi)\otimes\varphi$ with $C_{\rm red}=\sum_i[A_i+\sum_xP^{(i)}_x\otimes(1+\gamma\theta_ix)\sigma_3\otimes(m_i+D_i)+\kappa_i\hat x_i\otimes X]$.
Gradients with a common field: $g_{m,i}=g_{\eta,i}=\gamma\theta_i$, $g_{\zeta,i}=0$, $\mathcal F_i=-\kappa_i\langle X\rangle$; class $\mathcal C$ iff $|\gamma|L\max(|\theta_1|,|\theta_2|)<1$.

With a common field: fall alike iff $\kappa_1\tau_1^2\theta_1=\kappa_2\tau_2^2\theta_2\neq0$; respond alike per label iff $\theta_1=\theta_2$, per distance iff $\theta_1/\kappa_1=\theta_2/\kappa_2$; both fall and response per distance iff in addition $\tau_1\kappa_1=\tau_2\kappa_2$; no condition contains $\gamma$.

Well defined: $\theta_1=\theta_2$, the value of $\theta_1/\theta_2$ and $\theta_1/d_{0,1}=\theta_2/d_{0,2}$; not well defined: the value of $\theta_i\gamma$, which shifts by $a\theta_i$ under $\Phi\to\Phi+a$.
Common coupling for the fall: $v_1^2\theta_1/d_{0,1}=v_2^2\theta_2/d_{0,2}$; common coupling for the clocks: $\theta_1/d_{0,1}=\theta_2/d_{0,2}$; they coincide iff $v_1=v_2$.
The relative factor of the two bodies is detectable iff the medium is read and $X$ is not diagonal in the places of the medium.

Under an equivalence with factors $a_i$: $\tau_i,m_i,\mathcal F_i,\kappa_i,d_{0,i}$ are divided by $a_i$, $\lambda_{0,i}\to a_i\lambda_{0,i}$, $g_{m,i},g_{\eta,i},g_{\zeta,i},\varrho_i$ are unchanged, $v_i\to v_i/a_i^2$, $\varrho_i/d_{0,i}\to a_i\varrho_i/d_{0,i}$, $A^{(i)}_{k,\sigma}\to A^{(i)}_{k,\sigma}/a_i^3$, $A^{(i)}_{k,+}/v_i^2\to a_iA^{(i)}_{k,+}/v_i^2$.

Every equivalence whose contract is again of the form of the setting has $F'_i=F_i/a_i+c_i$, so $C'^{\rm eff}_i=C^{\rm eff}_i/a_i+c_i$ and $\kappa'_i(X'-\langle X'\rangle)=\kappa_i(X-\langle X\rangle)/a_i$.

Falling alike, $v_1=v_2$ and equal response per distance are the same in every equivalent description only if the relative factor is detectable; equal response per label and the relation (4.24) of each type are the same in every case.

With the medium not read, $a_1/a_2=\sqrt{v_1/v_2}$ gives $v'_1=v'_2$, with $A'^{(1)}/A'^{(2)}=(v_2/v_1)^{3/2}A^{(1)}/A^{(2)}$, $\varrho'_i=\varrho_i$ and the ratio of the responses per distance multiplied by $\sqrt{v_1/v_2}$.
An equivalent description in which the two types fall alike exists iff each type falls level-independently and $g_{\eta,1}g_{\eta,2}>0$.

With the convention of equal maximal speeds, falling alike and equal response per distance become one invariant statement: $A^{(1)}/v_1^{3/2}=A^{(2)}/v_2^{3/2}\neq0$, that is $\varrho_1\sqrt{\tau_1/\kappa_1}=\varrho_2\sqrt{\tau_2/\kappa_2}\neq0$, with level-independent fall in each type.

definitions.name: Response per label of the clock of a type
Background acceleration from rest of a level and a branch
Two types fall alike from rest (FA)
Clocks respond alike per label (RL) and per distance (RD)
Fall coupling of a type to a common field
Invariant fall number of a type under separate re-timings

open_issues: Item 5: with Model D body contracts the effective gradient is F_i = −κ_i⟨X⟩, so the level-independence is exact only for ⟨X⟩ = 0; for ⟨X⟩ ≠ 0 it holds at the leading order in κ_i, and the conditions on the six numbers carry this qualification.

The classification (8.17) covers the equivalent descriptions that are again of the form of the setting (class C, linear profiles, one operator of the medium, at least three positions); for an equivalent contract outside this form, for example with a non-constant term Δ of (5.19), the statements of (8.18) are not defined here.
All results are of first order in the gradients, from rest and at leading order in the records; the fall in motion, the lattice terms and a field that is not sharp are out of scope.
The convention of equal maximal speeds in (8.21) is a choice; whether anything in the language selects it belongs to criterion 10.

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions (d0 ~ 1/λ, v ~ 1/λ², A ~ 1/λ³) and the equivalence (5.20) with a1 = a2 = s, which reproduces the unit change (8.3) and leaves every statement of (8.18) unchanged

Two types with identical data: v1 = v2, equal responses, and falling alike reduces to the level-independence condition with a non-zero gradient, as (8.8) states; with the medium not read a description without equal fall still exists
One clock gradient set to zero: the fall of that type vanishes, falling alike fails, and no equivalent description with equal fall exists, in agreement with (8.20)
